title: Gummy Stem Blight on Melons(Watermelon and Cantaloupes)

Header: Gummy Stem Blight on Melons(Watermelon and Cantaloupes)

Prevention: Plant varieties that can withstand the disease eg. 'Micky- Lee'.
Avoid overcrowding of field by observing planting distances: - Watermelon -5ft x 5ft.
Gummy stem disease is seed borne.
Purchase treated seed from reputable sources
Cantaloupe with crops that does not belong to the cucurbits family growing melons only 1 year in 3 where possible.
The fungus survives on infected crops residues.
Remove and burn plant residues from field
This disease can enter plants through damage caused by mechanical wounds and insect injuries.
Control insects (aphids and whiteflies) in the field and avoid causing damage to vine.
Melon cultivation should be restricted to the dry season only.
Mulch using plastic or dry grass to reduce the spread of spores
Monitoring: Regular scouting of field at least twice a week.
Gummy stem disease affects the leaves, stems and fruits of melons.
Observe leaves for circular, dark brown to black spots that are sometimes surrounded with yellow halo.
In the later stage of the disease these spots dry up, become cracked and fall off.
Infected stem develop canker which produce a gummy red or brown gummy fluid.
Direct control actions should be taken as soon as the disease is identified.
Direct Control: Overhead irrigation should be avoided. if overhead irrigation is used, irrigate in the morning
Prune and burn affected leaves and vines
Restrictions: Use fungicides which contain active ingredients such as
Bellis - (Boscalid 25.2% w/w and pyraclastrobin 12.8% w/w), rate of application 2.5-5.0g/gal.
Very toxic to aquatic life with long lasting effects.
To avoid risks to human health and the environment, comply with the instructions for use.
WHO CLASS III. unlikely to present acute harm
